moduleAmendment.destination: Update finite evidence correctly, then choose an action under an explicit payoff/utility criterion and value a specified observation channel.
moduleAmendment.gate: The original 24-session updating core retains its historical review. The four decision-bridge sessions are a new builder-checked candidate; all 28 require their own evidence. Fixed tasks alone do not certify unseen transfer or retention.

sessions.title: From posterior probabilities to actions
sessions.focus: Derive an action threshold and choose using posterior expected payoff.
sessions.purpose: Close the M05→M06 finite decision handoff through an explicit, checkable construction.
sessions.centralCapability: Derive an action threshold and choose using posterior expected payoff.
sessions.principalObstacle: Treating a posterior as an action rule without a loss/payoff model.
entryPrerequisites: M05-S18–S19 supplied utility and certainty equivalents
M06-S06–S11 Bayes and positive evidence normalization
requiredOwnership: Compare all constant actions under the prior.
Normalize the observed-signal posterior from the given channel.
Derive the payoff-dependent action threshold including the tie.
Choose among actions using their posterior values.
State information timing, criterion and model limits.
sessions.applicationScope: Finite states/actions with an explicit prior, observation channel, decision timing and supplied payoff/utility criterion.
sessions.transferScope: A changed information or decision structure; no distribution, optimal-control or utility-representation theorem is assumed.
inScope: Finite posterior action choice with supplied payoff or utility table
EVPI and EVSI under a specified finite observation channel
Nonnegative gross information value when information can be ignored
Acquisition costs in the correct units and information timing
sessions.exitCondition: Solve both public tasks with the conditioning model and the action criterion visible; demonstrate an unfamiliar delayed variant before a mastery claim.
sessions.lesson: An updated belief and a decision answer different questions. First state the action set, outcome payoffs, information available before action, and criterion. For two states H,Hᶜ, the expected payoff of action a at belief q is q r(a,H)+(1−q)r(a,Hᶜ). Compare all feasible actions; a .5 cutoff has no special status unless the payoffs imply it. A supplied utility table is averaged in utility units, not money. Worked example: prior P(H)=.2, a signal has likelihoods .6 under H and .1 under Hᶜ. Its mass is .2 and the positive-signal posterior is .6. Action X pays (7,−3), action Y pays (0,0). X is better iff 10q−3≥0, so its threshold is .3. Before the signal Y beats X's −1; after the positive signal X has value 3. This conclusion assumes the stated channel, timing and payoff criterion; it is not a consequence of Bayes alone. Guided check: With payoffs (3,−1) versus (0,0), derive the threshold and explain why a belief .3 can favor the risky action.
sessions.codingExtension: Enumerate states and signals using exact rational arithmetic. Compare a signal-contingent policy with every constant action; verify that ignoring a free signal remains feasible. Coding is an optional cross-check and does not replace the proof.

sessions.focus: Compute EVPI and prove gross information value is nonnegative.
sessions.purpose: Close the M05→M06 finite decision handoff through an explicit, checkable construction.
sessions.centralCapability: Compute EVPI and prove gross information value is nonnegative.
sessions.principalObstacle: Swapping a maximum with an expectation or valuing information after its outcome is known.
requiredOwnership: Compute the best prior action value.
Construct state-contingent actions after perfect revelation.
Compare gross EVPI with an acquisition cost in the same units.
Prove nonnegative EVPI from statewise inequalities.
Distinguish a pre-observation value from a realized conditional action value.

sessions.lesson: Before purchasing information, compare policies at the same prior and decision time. Let V0=max_a Σ_h p(h)r(a,h). Perfect revelation before action permits choosing a different action in each state: VPI=Σ_h p(h)max_a r(a,h). EVPI=VPI−V0. For every constant action, the statewise maximum is at least its state payoff; multiply by nonnegative probabilities and sum, then maximize the constant action. This proves EVPI≥0. It is an upper bound on gross value of a signal that only reveals information about the same state and does not alter actions or payoffs. Worked example: P(H)=.5; X=(6,−2), Y=(1,1). V0=2, VPI=.5·6+.5·1=3.5, EVPI=1.5. A fee 1.2 in the same net monetary units leaves benefit .3; a fee 2 would not be worthwhile. With nonlinear wealth utility, a monetary fee must enter terminal wealth before utility is evaluated; do not subtract currency from utility units. Guided check: Why can informative free revelation have zero value if one action is already best in every state?
sessions.codingExtension: Enumerate states and signals using exact rational arithmetic. Compare a signal-contingent policy with every constant action; verify that ignoring a free signal remains feasible. Coding is an optional cross-check and does not replace the proof.

sessions.purpose: Close the M05→M06 finite decision handoff through an explicit, checkable construction.

requiredOwnership: Normalize every positive-mass report and its posterior.
Construct an optimal report-contingent action policy.

Verify the information bounds under a common action/payoff model.
Price acquisition in correct units and state assumptions.

sessions.lesson: Specify the entire reporting channel P(s|h). For each report of positive mass, normalize P(h|s), then choose an action. The pre-observation signal value is VS=Σ_s P(s)max_a Σ_h P(h|s)r(a,h); zero-mass reports contribute zero and require no conditional. EVSI=VS−V0. A free signal can be ignored, so VS≥V0; each report's conditional maximum is no larger than its conditional expectation of the statewise maximum, so VS≤VPI. Both claims need the same feasible actions and payoffs, pre-action observation and no forced use. Worked example: prior .5, signal accuracy .8 in both states, X=(4,−4), Y=(0,0). Both reports have mass .5. Posteriors are .8 and .2; choose X after + (value 2.4), Y after −. VS=1.2, V0=0, EVSI=1.2 and EVPI=2. A monetary fee .7 leaves net gain .5. Guided check: Why does valuing the signal at 2.4 ignore half the reports? How does a fee change terminal wealth before nonlinear utility is averaged?

sessions.title: Integrated information-policy audit
sessions.focus: Build a finite information model and distinguish informativeness from decision value.
sessions.purpose: Close the M05→M06 finite decision handoff through an explicit, checkable construction.
sessions.centralCapability: Build a finite information model and distinguish informativeness from decision value.
sessions.principalObstacle: Assuming an informative signal must change the best action or have positive value.
entryPrerequisites: M04-S27 reporting protocol; M05-S24 criterion discipline
requiredOwnership: Validate and normalize a finite joint state/report law.
Derive posteriors and an admissible conditional policy including ties.
Compute baseline, sample-information value and perfect-information bound.
Distinguish informative reporting from positive decision value.
State acquisition, protocol and criterion limits without inventing information.

sessions.lesson: An information-policy audit makes the joint state/report law visible, checks normalization, identifies the pre-observation baseline, then checks every posterior action. Informativeness need not produce positive decision value: an updated belief may remain on the same side of every action threshold. Worked example: prior .5; A=(5,−1), B=(0,0). A is optimal for beliefs above 1/6. A channel producing posteriors .4 and .6 with equal report masses is informative, but A remains optimal after both reports. Its pre-observation value remains 2, hence EVSI=0. Perfect revelation still has value .5·5=2.5, so EVPI=.5. An unspecified reporter protocol does not determine a posterior: a state-sensitive reporter and an independent reporter can produce the same marginal frequency but different joint laws. Guided check: Construct a channel whose reports alter beliefs without altering optimal actions. Verify VS directly by summing joint state/report masses, rather than treating a report as a new prior.

T22V3::ARC502::S25-M@1.prompt: Prior P(H)=1/4. A positive signal has likelihood 4/5 under H and 1/5 under Hᶜ and is observed before action. Operate pays 12 under H and −8 under Hᶜ; wait pays 1 in either state. Maximize expected monetary payoff. Compare actions before observation, compute the positive-signal mass and posterior, derive the operate/wait threshold including ties, choose after the signal using both values, and state the timing/model/criterion limits.

T22V3::ARC502::S25-T@1.prompt: A screening model has P(H)=3/5, with report R likelihood 1/2 under H and 3/4 under Hᶜ. Approve pays 4 under H and −10 under Hᶜ; hold pays 0 in either state. Under expected-money maximization, compare prior values, compute P(R) and P(H|R), derive the approval threshold including ties, choose after R, and explain why a probability-only approval rule is inadequate.

T22V3::ARC502::S26-M@1.prompt: P(H)=3/10. Action A pays (15,−5) in H,Hᶜ; B pays (2,2). Use expected monetary payoff. Compute the best prior action, construct the perfect-information policy and its pre-observation value, compute EVPI and decide whether a fee 4 is worth paying. Prove EVPI≥0 for arbitrary finite states/actions by a statewise comparison, and explain why the acquisition decision is made before revelation.

T22V3::ARC502::S26-T@1.prompt: Three states have probabilities (1/5,3/10,1/2). Actions A,B,C pay (6,−2,0), (0,4,−1), (1,1,1). Maximize expected money. Compare all prior actions; find an optimal action after perfect state revelation; compute EVPI and the net value at fee 2. Prove the nonnegativity inequality for this setup and explain why looking only at the most favorable revelation misprices the information.

T22V3::ARC502::S27-M@1.prompt: P(H)=2/5. Signal + has likelihood 3/4 under H and 1/4 under Hᶜ; − is its complement and arrives before action. Play pays (10,−6); safe pays (0,0). Maximize expected money. Compute both report masses/posteriors, choose after each report, compute the best prior value, VS and EVSI, compare with EVPI, and decide whether to buy at monetary fee 3/2. State the assumptions behind 0≤EVSI≤EVPI.

T22V3::ARC502::S27-T@1.prompt: A finite model has P(H)=1/3. Report R likelihood is 1/2 under H and 1/4 under Hᶜ; N is its complement. The supplied utility table is A=(2,−1), B=(0,0). Reports arrive before action and may be ignored. Normalize both reports; choose the utility-maximizing policy; compute V0, VS, EVSI and EVPI in utility units. A seller asks a fee of 0.1 monetary units but supplies no wealth-to-utility model. Prove the information bounds and say exactly whether the purchase decision is identifiable.

T22V3::ARC502::S28-M@1.prompt: The joint state/report table is P(H,+)=3/10, P(H,−)=1/5, P(Hᶜ,+)=1/10, P(Hᶜ,−)=2/5. The report is available before action. A pays (8,−4), B=(0,0), with expected-money maximization and optional use of the report. Validate the law and prior, derive both posteriors and optimal actions including ties, compute V0, VS, EVSI and EVPI, decide at fee1/10, and explain how the report can be informative with zero decision value. Explain why the same report words from an unspecified reporter do not determine the same posterior.

T22V3::ARC502::S28-T@1.prompt: Three states have prior (1/5,3/10,1/2). The specified reporter gives R with conditional probabilities (1/2,3/5,4/5); N is the complement. Act pays (9,2,−3), safe pays (1,1,1). Under expected-money maximization with pre-action optional reports, build the joint table, normalize both posteriors, choose conditional actions, compute V0, VS, EVSI and EVPI, and decide at fee3/5. Explain why knowing only P(R), rather than this conditional channel, would not identify the posterior policy.

T22V3::ARC502::S25-M@1.reference: Before observation: operate=−3, wait=1. P(+)=7/20; P(H|+)=4/7. Operate=20q−8 versus wait=1; operate iff q≥9/20, tie at equality. After +, operate=24/7, wait=1, so operate. The rule uses supplied net monetary payoffs, expected-money maximization and an observation available before action; a posterior alone does not justify a recommendation outside this model.

rubric.criterion: Prior values −3 and 1 and the choice wait are derived.
Signal mass 7/20 and posterior 4/7 are normalized.
Threshold 9/20 and tie case are derived from the payoff comparison.
Posterior values 24/7 and 1 justify operate.
Conclusion states criterion, pre-action observation and conditional model scope.
